subject: Biotechnology
title: Cancer Resistance Mechanisms
description: Learn Cancer Resistance Mechanisms in one minute.

hook.text: Targeted therapy works beautifully — until it stops. Cancer evolves resistance, and genomics reveals how.

buildup.text: Gatekeeper mutations change the drug-binding site — the targeted protein still works but the drug cannot bind.

discovery.text: Bypass pathway activation lets cancer grow through alternative signals — blocking one path opens another.

twist.text: Serial biopsies during treatment reveal resistance mutations in real time — allowing rapid therapy switching.

climax.text: Osimertinib was designed to overcome T790M resistance — a second-generation drug for the resistant mutation.

punchline.text: Cancer adapts — genomics keeps up, guiding the next move.

quiz.question: What is a gatekeeper mutation in cancer resistance?
options: A mutation that prevents cancer cells from entering the bloodstream
A change in the drug-binding site that blocks the drug without affecting the protein's function
A mutation in immune cells that prevents them from attacking cancer

details.summary: Cancers develop resistance to targeted therapies through mutations in drug targets, activation of bypass signaling pathways, and epigenetic changes. Genomic analysis of resistant tumors reveals these mechanisms, enabling rational selection of second-line therapies and combination strategies.
details.whyItMatters: Drug resistance is the primary reason cancer treatments eventually fail. Understanding resistance mechanisms through genomic profiling enables oncologists to anticipate and overcome resistance, converting fatal relapses into manageable disease
takeaways: Target mutations, pathway bypass, and epigenetic changes drive resistance
Serial tumor genomic profiling detects resistance mechanisms as they emerge
Combination therapies can preempt resistance by blocking escape routes

faq.question: How do cancers become resistant to targeted drugs?
faq.answer: The most common mechanism is mutation in the drug target itself, preventing drug binding. Alternatively, tumors activate alternative signaling pathways that bypass the blocked target entirely.

faq.question: Can genomic profiling predict resistance before it happens?
faq.answer: Liquid biopsies monitoring circulating tumor DNA can detect resistance mutations weeks to months before clinical progression. This enables proactive treatment switches. Predicting which resistance mechanism will emerge based on the initial tumor profile is an active research area.
